headlines.title: FDA approves ‘game-changing’ pancreatic cancer drug
headlines.description: In a late-stage trial, people who got Revolution Medicines’ Rasonque, or daraxonrasib, lived about twice as long as people who got standard care.

headlines.title: FDA approves breakthrough pancreatic cancer treatment
headlines.description: The Food and Drug Administration approved a breakthrough pancreatic cancer treatment, found to double survival to thirteen months compared to people who just got chemotherapy. It's called Rasonque, and it's approved for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer. NBC News' Anne Thompson reports.

headlines.title: An infant was one of the two measles-related deaths in Pennsylvania
headlines.description: One of the two people who recently died of measles in Pennsylvania was an infant, the state Health Department said. The department announced that two unvaccinated residents had died of measles, the first measles-related deaths in the U.S. this year and the first in Pennsylvania in 35 years. NBC News' Erika Edwards reports.

headlines.title: FDA approves groundbreaking new drug for pancreatic cancer
headlines.description: The Food and Drug Administration approved a groundbreaking new oral drug for pancreatic patients suffering from the most aggressive form of the disease. Daraxonrasib, which targets a mutation in a gene called KRAS, doubled the survival time in patients who participated in the trial.

headlines.title: Health Officials Report 2 Measles-Related Deaths in Pennsylvania
headlines.description: Health officials say two people have died in Pennsylvania after being infected with measles. Both of the individuals from Lancaster County were unvaccinated. They are the first measles-related deaths in the United States this year.
